articleTitle: The Effect of Photovoltaic Penetration on Frequency Response of Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Currently solar photovoltaic that is integrated into the grid has significantly increased the capacity. High photovoltaic penetration on the grid has an effect on the reliability and stability system. This is due to the nature of the fluctuative photovoltaic generation. This paper analyzed the effect of fluctuative photovoltaic generation on system frequency and determined the maximum level of photovoltaic penetration integrated to a 20 kV distribution grid which is in accordance with Indonesian grid code. A matlab simulink is used to simulate the solar photovoltaic integrated into the distribution grid which the photovoltaic penetration are varied to be 25%., 20%., 15% and 10% of peak load. In this simulation., the photovoltaic plant is not equipped by energy storage system that aim to see the frequency response system naturally. One of the grid code that must be complied is to keep the frequency system in the range of 47.5 to 52 Hz. Based on the simulation., photovoltaic penetration of 25% results the lowest frequency of 46.6 Hz so that the penetration is not permitted to integrate into the grid. While the maximum level of photovoltaic penetration that might be allowed to integrate is 20% which results in the lowest frequency of 48 Hz.

articleTitle: Simulation of PV - Biogas Integration on Hybrid Power Plant using HOMER: Study Case of Superior Livestock Breeding Center and Forage of Animal Feed (BBPTU - HPT) Baturraden
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: The use of renewable energy in the last few years has increased although it is still expensive. This is might be caused by the increasing of public awareness to the environment. Hybrid systems are one way to reduce the price of renewable energy. This paper discusses the hybrid of photovoltaic (PV) and biogas as renewable energy power generation that is located in Superior Livestock Breeding Center and Forage of Animal Feed (BBPTU-HPT) Baturraden. The electricity generated from the system will be used to supply the electricity in the cattle pen such as for lighting, water sprayers and grass chopper machine. Electricity needs in cattle pen are 0.8kW at the lowest load and 12kW at the highest load. The potential for renewable energy at this location is 126.74-220.42 kWh per day from biogas and the solar radiation potential is 4.75 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/d. Homer simulations will be used to determine the combination of generation at the lowest price. The simulation results showed that the lowest generation price is $ 0.25. This value is still more expensive compared to the price of electricity from PLN which is $ 0.1.

articleTitle: An Evalyuation of TEC and TEG Characterization for a Road Thermal Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: This paper presented a characterization of TEC and TEG for a road thermal energy harvesting system (RTEHs) purposes. Five modules are chosen randomly from unknown manufacturer to reputable ones where the prices range from low to high used to find the potential thermoelectric module (TEM) for RTEHs according to Malaysia's climate. The experiment confirms the previous work where TEC work efficiently for lower temperature <;75 °C for power generation than TEG. The study found that size and the configuration placement of the module, influence the generated output greatly. By cascading it, module on top of module, the module able to generate, 2.3194 V at Tc = 31.653 °C, Th = 61.335 °C and ΔT = 29.77°C.

articleTitle: A Single-Wire Method of Coupling Interface in Capacitive Power Transfer for Electric Vehicle Wireless Charging System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach of coupling interface configuration on capacitive power transfer (CPT) for electric vehicle wireless charging system. CPT has several advantages in use of wireless charging system for short range application such as electric vehicle. One of the advantages is flexibility of coupling interface. Two-pairs of plate usually used to acquire electric field work in order to deliver some amount of designated power. This paper studies a single-wire coupling interface for EV charging system. Simulation has been done in SPICE software with the consideration of parasitic components appearing in the system. As the result, at 3.3 kW output power delivered, the coupling voltage and chassis voltage were measured at 24,720 V and 114V, respectively. This level is obtained when the coupling and chassis capacitances are 1.1 pF and 442 pF, correspondingly. The values are extracted by the electric field simulation on a normal size car.

articleTitle: State of Charge Monitoring System of Electric Vehicle Using Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: The purpose of this research was to design a state of charge (SoC) monitoring device and to understand the effect of temperature on SoC during trials of an electric golf cart. A fuzzy logic system was used to design the prototype SoC monitoring system. The source of the SoC fuzzy logic system was repeated real-time current (I), voltage (V), and temperature (T) measurement during battery charge and discharge. For the charging data, the battery was charged with a constant current (~15A) and the variable data (V and T) were measured using a monitoring device until the battery was fully charged. Then, the variable discharge data (I, V, and T) were captured as the electric car was being used to move around the campus area. It was found that temperature affects the beginning and end of charging time for 10 to 20% of the SoC value. However, during battery discharge, the temperature randomly affects voltage due to the random power consumption by the electric motor.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Crossflow Turbine Prototype for Picohydro Scale
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: This paper discusses the design and analysis of Crossflow turbine with picohydro scale. This turbine can be applied to river flow with small water flow rate and low head. This picohydro turbine specification is about 500 W with 4 m net head and a maximum flow rate of 0.018 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/s. Prototypes of Crossflow turbine were tested at the power plant laboratory owned by TELIMEK-LIPI. The test is performed with both the flow rate and head conditions that are set permanently or close to the design value. The maximum real power produced by the turbine can be seen from the electrical power produced by the generator. The generator then flows into an electric load. The test results are obtained in the form of rotational graphs for power and real power graphs for efficiency. The turbine test results obtained have an efficiency of 82.20% with a real output power of 346 W.

articleTitle: Solar Air Heater for Preheating The Air of Broiler House
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Theoretical studies have been conducted on the application of solar air heater for preheating the air of broiler house. The air heating system of broiler house was use a gas air heater and equipped with rocks bed as the thermal storage medium. The study was conducted for the broiler house with the capacity of 30,000 chickens, which is a house with a size of 100 m x 12 m and has two floors, each floor with a capacity of 15,000 chickens. This study aims to determine the potential amount of savings the use of LPG and operating costs of heating chicken coops during the brooding period (2 weeks of starting the chicken farm) on a chicken coop that using the additional solar air heater and heat storage medium compared to air gas heater only. The study shows that the proposed heating system can save gas usage as much as 613.06 kg per harvest cycle. However, the proposed heating system requires additional electrical energy to operate the fan/blower, amounting to 700.66 kWh per crop cycle. The operational cost savings of the proposed heating system is IDR 6,066,358, - per crop cycle (the calculation basis as of November 2015).

articleTitle: Traffic Simulation in an Intersection by Using Integrated Vissim-MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: This paper describes the coupling scheme between Matlab and commercial tool for traffic simulation, PTV Vissim, which can be integrated and performed in realtime simulation. A step-by-step procedure of the scheme by using amenities that provided by the tool, Vissim Component Object Model (COM) interface, is also presented. This research succeed to read and store the outcomes in. txt file. These outcomes are the number of vehicles that enter and exit an intersection, also the queue length of vehicles in an intersection each road.

articleTitle: A Dynamical Model of Full Bridge LLC Resonant Converter Which Incorporates Power Loss Coefficients for Controller Design
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: DC-DC converters play important role in smart grids and electric vehicles. A practical model is needed for effective controller design of full bride LLC resonant converter, a topology of DC-DC converter. This paper proposes a new practical model of full bridge LLC resonant converter which incorporates power loss coefficients. Power losses due to MOSFET on-resistance, equivalent serial resistance (ESR), and voltage drop of diode are expressed using power loss coefficients. A practical linear model in state space equation is obtained using Jacobian matrices. A physical model inSimulink/Simscape Electrical<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>environment is builtbased on a prototype of LLC converter which has nominal input voltage of 120 V, nominal output voltage of 240 V, and nominal switching frequency of 100 kHz. In order to validate the proposed practical model, transient responses comparison between the practical linear model and the physical model was carried out through computer simulation. From the simulation results, it can be concluded that the proposed practical linear model represents well dynamics of the physical model. Therefore, the proposed practical linear model can be used for controller design in an effective manner based on analytical approach.

articleTitle: A Simple And Implementation of Interleaved Boost Converter For Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Currently the DC-DC Converter discusses the interleaved boost converter for renewable energy applications. The renewable energy used is solar panels. Interleaved boost converter is used as an inverter source. The interleaved output voltage and inverter output voltage is controlled using fuzzy logic. The final load of the system is home appliances such as lamps and water pumps. In this paper present implementation of the interleaved boost converter and SPWM inverter for renewable energy.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of Closed Loop Buck Converter to Supply Constant DC Load for Single Solar PV Panel
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Buck converter is one of the power electronics circuits used as voltage lowering regulator. This paper addresses the modeling and simulation of buck converter to supply a low power dc load based on standalone of solar power system without using the battery. Modeling includes the characteristics of a single solar PV panel as input voltages that tend to vary due to the influence of irradiation and temperature. The converter was equipped by closed loop PI controller based on voltage control mode to keep the output voltage constant of 12 Volt. Modeling was performed and simulated using PSIM. The results show that in the irradiation variation 600-1500 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> generate the PV voltage of 12.1 - 18.9 Volt as the input voltage. From its input, the buck converter was able to maintain the output voltage of 12 Volt with an error of ±0.83 %.

articleTitle: Working Fluid Selection for Electricity Production Using Organic Rankine Cycle with Heat Source Temperature of 100°C
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) generates electricity at low temperature heat sources; therefore, this system produces a low performance. Working fluid selection is important to determine a better ORC system performance. This paper discusses working fluid selection for electricity production using ORC system with heat source temperature of 100°C. The analysis was carried out by varying organic working fluid with constant temperature and volume flow rate of the heat source. R123, R245fa, R141b, R227ea, R134a and n-pentane are selected to be analyzed as organic working fluid. All of the selected working fluid are analyzed through energy and exergy balance to determine each of their performances. Net power and thermal efficiency are performance result from energy balance analysis, while exergy balance analyzes exergy input and exergy efficiency as a performance result. The analysis shows that R141b as isentropic fluid type results in the highest performance, and R227ea as wet (almost isentropic) fluid type obtains the lowest performance.

articleTitle: Product Cost Calculation of Piezoelectric Generator as an Energy Harvester
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: A piezoelectric generator has been developed as a renewable energy harvester. As a new product, the product cost estimation must be performed. This paper proposes a methodology for product cost calculation of the developed product using full costing method. The calculation result shows that the electrical component in terms of piezoelectric transducer is dominant about 41.31%of total product cost followed by mechanical components of 28.25%, labor cost of 25.74 %, and overhead cost of 4.69%. The calculated product cost that obtained is expected to be a consideration for developing the piezoelectric generator.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting from a Crane System by a Piezoelectric Energy Harvester: Two Concentrated Moving Forces Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Design of a piezoelectric energy harvester (PEH) for a crane system is developed. This design employs linear vibration of a crane framework which deforms when the trolley and payload traversing on the top beam of the crane framework. The top beam is connected to a piezoelectricity lever-arm mechanism as a PEH through spring. Vibration of the crane framework becomes excitation force for the piezoelectricity lever-arm mechanism. It is then converted into useful electrical energy. The research results show the electric power can be harvested up to 37.5 W for one PEH with a span of 12 m of the top beam of the crane framework at the trolley speed of 1 m/s, and the total mass of 1200 kg.

articleTitle: Study of Gray Code Implementation for Single Phase Inverter Short Circuit Protection
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Inan electronic circuit, short circuit protection can be done by using passive and active method. The active method is usually using current sensor and/or thermo sensor while the passive method is using trigger design for power circuit such dead time delay trigger or digitally interlock trigger for high side and low side. Dead time delay method can increase the total harmonic distortion (THD) while the interlock method must add more components. This paper discusses the design of Gray code for passive short circuit protection. Gray code is widely used in the field of communications technology, mechanical engineering, and digital data processing because the Gray code can minimize errors. The Gray code converts an integer value, represented as a voltage, into a series of pulses in digital form. In inverter design based on microcontroller, calculations to generate AC modulation is done in the microcontroller. This increases programming complexity and amount of coding downloaded to the microcontroller chip while the capacity of the flash memory in the microcontroller is limited. In turn, this makes program execution time is longer. This paper discusses the design of a single phase inverter using unipolar method with modulation of the sine wave and the triangular wave is done outside the microcontroller using data processing software application (Microsoft Excel) and short circuit protection using gray code modulation.

articleTitle: Computational Fluid Dynamic Simulation on Bladeless Fan as Active Cooling Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: In the current research, Heat is the main problem for the electrical components and battery of electric bus. It has a high potential to shorten the lifetime of the component, especially battery while charged at stationer condition and controller while operating at high load. This study was aimed to investigate the characteristic of the bladeless fan as active cooling implementation for electronic component and battery inside a chair of an electric bus by using CFD simulation. Analysis of the performance and flow inside the fan system were obtained by aerodynamic investigation. A cross section of airfoil profile was used in order to design the optimal bladeless fan. The inlet air speed, diagonal airfoil ratio, slit thickness of outlet airflow, and distance ration couple of airfoils was varied. The result showed that fourdiagonal value ratios had reached maximum value discharge ration and it had increased significantly when the outlet thickness decreased. Overall inlet slit thickness variation was indicated that this variable is the most influent parameter on the Bladeless aerodynamic fan performance.

articleTitle: Design of Three-Phase Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Generator Double-Side Internal Rotor for High-Speed Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: One of the important factors to support the successful development of a region is strongly influenced by the availability of electrical energy. The electrical energy is produced by a generator that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. The axial flux permanent magnet generator (AFPMG) is a generator with the direction of the magnetic flux in the air gap parallel to the shaft of the generator. The generator process design will be discussed in this paper which is divided into four steps and was calculated by using analytical and numerical methods. The generator is designed to produce the output power of 20,000 watts, terminal voltage of 220 volts, frequency of 50 Hz, and rotor speed of 3,000 rpm. In the preliminary stages of the design process based on the analytical method, the output variables and the generator performance will be known manually. To ensure the accuracy of the results of the analytical method including the magnitude of the output variables and the generator performances, a software of two-dimension finite element software is used. The results of the validation show that the magnitude of the magnetic circuits resulted by the analytical method is able to distribute the magnetic flux without causing saturation to any part of its circuit. At a constant speed of 3,000 rpm, the variation of the current line affects the performance of the generator. When the generator is loaded with the resistive load under the full-load condition, the efficiency is 89.62%, the voltage regulation is 4.02 %, and the output power is 29,116.74143 watts.

articleTitle: Study of Combustion and Emission Characteristic of Homogenous Charge Compression Ignition Engine Using Computational Fluid Dynamic
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Numerical methods are used to predict HCCI engine performance, which is more cost-effective than experimentation alone. Specific strategies used numerical methods in HCCI an engine with three-dimensional modelling of combustion on 1 cylinder HCCI combustion engine fuelled by Diesel fuel is described in this paper. The 3 D model is performed on AVL Fire software. The combustion with basic parameters including different start time of Injections (SOI) with the same duration of combustion (BD), indicating pressure in chamber and emissions (Nitric Oxide and soot) were evaluate. The modelling results show that the highest value of pressure in the combustion chamber on the HCCI method was achieved at a pressure of 107 bar 360 deg CA, while in conventional combustion methods it was achieved at 72 bar 363 deg CA. On the other hand the highest peak heat transfer rate is 127 J / deg at 10 deg BTDC, whereas for conventional method occurs at 32 J / deg at 1deg ATDC. So there is a shift of heat transfer toward to BTDC before TDC, due to the already homogeneous fuel in the HCCI method. The combustion process in HCCI engines increases emissions with high NO emissions and reduces Soot emissions.

articleTitle: Torsional Vibration Simulation of The Crankshaft Based on AVL Excite Designer
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: This paper discusses about torsional vibration simulation of the crankshaft which is one of the important component of internal combustion engine. Torsional vibration simulation of the crankshaft is an important stage during development of the crankshaft design. In this study, a four-cylinder, four-stroke inline gasoline engine's crankshaft, with bore and stroke 86 mm, was modelled using Solidworks and AVL Excite Designer. In the first steps design, three-dimentional model of crankshaft was built using Solidworks software which is used to obtain value of moment of inertia of each component of cranktrain and was inputed to AVL Excite Designer. In the next steps, in AVL Excite Designer, shaft and torsional modeller as a actual crankshaft. In this simulation external loading was taken from data base AVL Excite Designer with variables load. The calculations reaction torque, torque of each element on the crankshaft, critical speed, moment of inertia, and shear stress of the crankshaft was resulted. The results obtained are used as valuable reference in the optimization and improvement to the crankshaft design.

articleTitle: Performance and Productivity Enhancements on Vertical Axis Wind Turbines with a Novel multi-stages Contra-rotating Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: This work presents the development of multi stages and contra-rotating (MSCR) vertical axis wind turbine (VAWT) an attempt to enhance its performance and energy productivity. The efforts are achieved by rising capture capability of the wind energy by additional captured area, doubled the generator rotation and enhance the number of blades facing the wind. The constructional design and experimental set up showed the effectiveness of the multi stages contra rotating technique on VAWT. The performance evaluation of the MSCR construction was obtained in some parameters such as the emf generator and the output power over some wind speeds. The systematic evaluation of these parameters deduced some achievements of the double-stages MSCR technique on VAWT system that can make almost four times amount of power output if it is compared with a single stage VAWT. Another advantage of the MSCR technique is in the energy productivity that can extract significant additional energy on the VAWT systems with every additional stage.

articleTitle: Prediction Performance Map of Radial Compressor for System Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: The expanding of application in renewable energy based on small power plants for remote area is more attractive due to global warming and climate change concern. The power plants can be improved by increasing wide-range operation, variation working fluids, and operating point in turbomachinery components, such as the radial compressor. In the early stage of the design system, it is not easy to find and determine the radial compressor performance map in the open literature. In this paper presents an empirical model and simulations for predicting performance map of the radial compressor. The models were carried out Casey-Robinson method combine with Lüdtke method. Furthermore, the models were implemented in Python and GT-Suite. The result shows a satisfying trend predicting curve performance map for the radial compressor. This adopted model can be support for acceleration in the early stage of the design of power plant base-on renewable energy such as Solar Hybrid micro-Gas Turbine (SHGT) system and Parabolic Dish Solar Collector (PDSC) system.

articleTitle: Optimal Complex Power Production Cost in the Electric Power Market
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Cost reduction issues have received serious attention from actors of power industries during the past decade in the power market mechanism. Appropriate management of reactive power is very essential for supporting power system security. Besides, it has also dominant effects on real energy losses. Furthermore, the reactive power can support the secure operation of the system as an ancillary service. However, most researches have focussed on a transaction of the reactive power in electricity markets. On the other hand, reactive power production of generating is highly dependent on the real power output and only absorbed by the local consumers. As a result, to accommodate a market and to maintain a secure operation of the system, a fair cost allocation method seems to be very essential. Appropriate pricing of reactive power as an ancillary service has been a challenging problem during the past decade. However, most methods proposed so far for reactive power pricing are essentially based on empirical approximations. In this paper, a new method for reducing active and reactive power cost allocations has been proposed. The method is based on optimal cost calculation, which will be imposed on generators producing reactive power. The proposed method is fair, accurate and realistic, simple and easy to be applicated in the power system. Application of the proposed method on IEEE 9-bus standard network confirms its validity and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Performance Prediction of Adsorption Self-Cooling Mobile Container
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Solar thermal cooling technology utilization such as adsorption cooling system has attracted researchers as an alternative to conventional vapor compression system. The adsorption cooling system can utilize low-grade heat as its power source. This paper presents a numerical simulation of a new conceptual design of adsorption self-cooling mobile container to predict its adsorption performance. The container was mathematically modeled to calculate and simulate cooling power, COP, SCP, and the lowest temperature that could be obtained. The design consists of four main components namely the adsorption chamber, valve system, refrigerant chamber, and cabin chamber. Comparison between silica gel-water and zeolite-water had been investigated. The results show that evaporator temperature profile of the system with zeolite-water is better than the other working pair. Minimum value of the evaporator temperature is 18.14°C with zeolite-water as the working pair. The average cooling power, COP, and SCP during adsorption process are 1.48 J, 0.014, 0.984 W/kg, respectively.

articleTitle: Influence of Plate Width at Plate Heat Exchanger Evaporator Design for Organic Rankine Cycle with Heat Source Temperature of 70°C
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Evaporator in Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) system is used to convert the working fluid phase of pump output from liquid to vapor as a turbine input. Evaporator performance has an effect to ORC performance. This paper discusses the design of Plate Heat Exchanger (PHE) type as ORC evaporator which is utilized to vaporize the working fluid (R227ea) liquid phase at temperature and pressure of 35°C and 10 bar into saturated vapor phase at temperature of 53.42°C. Water was used as heating fluid with temperature and flow rate of 70°C and 2806 kg/h. PHE was designed by determining the constant and independent variables of PHE dimensions, calculating evaporator capacity, estimating the overall heat transfer coefficient, calculating heat transfer area and the pressure drop. The independent variable is PHE plate width(0.15m, 0.30m, and 0.45 m). The design result that the rise of plate width will increase total heat transfer area (1.44 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 1.62 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 1.89 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively). In the other side, the rise of plate width will decrease the total pressure drop to 0.13 bar, 0.04 bar, 0.02 bar (R227ea side) and 1.28 bar, 0.43 bar, 0.24 bar (water side).

articleTitle: Emission Control Strategy on GCI Engines Fueled with Biodiesel Blended in Gasoline
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Emission control strategy on GCI engines fueled with 5% by volume of biodiesel blended in gasoline was conducted in this study. The study was conducted using a 1-cylinder DI-CI engine. The engine was fueled with 5% by volume of biodiesel blended in gasoline. GCI combustion with the pilot, and main direct injections were applied in this study. Various EGR rate and intake pressure were also adapted to explore their effects on combustion and exhaust pollution control of the CI engines. It is found that gasoline-biodiesel blend with GCI combustion mode and various parameters especially EGR and intake boosting rate takes effect on the improvement of combustion characteristics which is closely related to HC, CO, NOx, and smoke emissions, respectively.

articleTitle: Evaluation of PMSM Performance by Different Modulation Strategies
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: A numerical simulation has been performed to examine the performance of inset rotor PMSM in terms of dynamic response, total harmonic distortion, torque and current ripple caused by three different modulation methods namely hysteresis current control (HCC), sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM) and space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM). In order to evaluate the performance of modulations, a quantitative analysis has been performed. The results show that SVPWM outweigh the other modulations.

articleTitle: A Study on Transfer Element in Single Switched Capacitor Battery Balancer System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Series-connected lead-acid battery is commonly used in a photovoltaic system. During charge-discharge cycle, each battery in the string would experience a voltage imbalance which leads to performance decay. Single switched capacitor battery balancer resolves this issue by transferring excessive charge from one battery to another. Therefore, the voltage imbalance will be at the acceptable limit. A transfer element is employed in this charge transfer process between batteries. In this paper, a battery balancer has been carried out by adopting balancing algorithm used in an LTC3305 chip. Simulation result shows that the use of the lead-acid battery as a transfer element is considerably more effective than the super-capacitor while speeding-up the balancing process.

articleTitle: An Initial Trial of Parabolic through Solar Collector System in Gunung Kidul, Yogyakarta, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: This paper discusses an initial trial of parabolic through solar collector (PTSC) in Gunung Kidul, Yogyakarta, Indonesia. The PTSC system consists of a solar collector, oil pump, and storage tank. The collector uses a parabolic type which consists of a concentrator, absorber and tracking system. The trial was conducted to determine the PTSC performance, such as collector capacity and storage capacity, and system efficiency. Solar intensity, temperature inlet and outlet of the working fluid in the storage tank was measured to determine PTSC performance. The collector has 3.5 m and 36 m of aperture width and parabolic length, with 1 m of focal distance. Palm oil is used as the working fluid and stored in a storage tank with a single type. The trial was carried out for two days with 30 minutes of interval time from 8:30 to 15:00 per day. The trial result shows that PTSC system produced 28.16 kW and 2.26 kW of collector capacity and storage capacity, and 8% efficiency on the first day. On the second day, PTSC produced 25.49 kW and 1.88 kW of collector capacity and storage capacity, and 7.4% efficiency.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Design of Electric Scooter for Sustainable Tourist Transportation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Research Centre for Electrical Power and Mechatronics, Indonesian Institute of Sciences (RCEPM-LIPI) has been conducting research on renewable energy in remote areas in Indonesia. The remote areas include rural area and small islands. The renewable energy has great potential to be used for transportation on a small tourist island. As such, in this article, we propose a re-design of an electric scooter from the originally designed for city transportation so that the new vehicle will be operable in the less developed infrastructure of a small island. The new design retains the original concept of simple and easy as it is considered suitable for recreational purposes. Ecotourism of a small island requires ecological, socio-cultural, and economic sustainability, therefore other than the eco-friendly renewable energy, the design should also promote greater interaction between the visiting tourists and the local population, and encourage local entrepreneur creativity to customize the scooter and gain greater economic value from tourism. The new design with its simplicity is expected to be able to accommodate these objectives. As the design is still at the preliminary stage, there are many further works necessary, from assessing technical feasibility, developing prototype and prototype testing.

articleTitle: Study on Energy Management System for Energy Saving on Semi Underground Rotary Parking Lot
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: The demand for parking space has been increased especially in urban area where office and commercial building densely emerged. With limited parking area on the ground, vertical parking system become one of the solutions to increase parking capacity within the same space as the conventional parking space. The proposed vertical parking in this research was focused on rotary parking since it requires the most minimum space of ground area. Furthermore, to reduce the high of the vertical parking, installing the vertical parking deep down into the underground has been another solution for increasing parking capacity. The parking system designed on this paper was installing the rotary parking semi underground which means the upper half of the rotary parking is still above the ground while the lower half of the rotary parking is buried under the ground level. The proposed parking lot was equipped with an energy storage system, power backup generator, intelligent control, and renewable energy source. Aside from the cost aspect in constructing this underground structure, this paper considers the energy saving scenarios which can be performed in this semi underground rotary parking system. Energy saving on this semi underground parking lot was facilitated using a smart inverter energy management system which was implanted with energy saving algorithm, intelligent control, spike absorber technique, and parking lots integration. The algorithm was calculating the intrusion from external factor, integrate it with internal sensor, and real time monitoring system. The result was shown to have 30 to 40 % energy saving which can be increased depend on certain parking structure and environment. It was concluded that additional equipment in semi underground rotary parking need a certain manner and algorithm so the parking operator could have a proper level of energy saving.

articleTitle: The Comparison Between Pre- and Post-Lunch Driving Performance among Morning Person Subjects during a Simulated Driving
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Driving fatigue has been widely reported to be one of the main causes of road traffic accidents. One type of driving fatigue is sleep-related fatigue associated with circadian rhythms, such as the phenomenon of a post-lunch dip in performance. In this study, we compared pre- and post-lunch driving performance in a simulated driving task using LCT Sim software. We measured reaction time, subjective sleepiness level (Karolinska Sleepiness Scale/KSS), and eye closure pattern (percentage of eye closure/PERCLOS). Participants were 12 healthy young adult males of morning person type. They performed 60 minutes of driving divided into three 20 minutes periods. From the 20 minutes period, all variables were averaged in every 5 minutes. Statistical analysis employed were Paired T-test, one way ANOVA with repeated measures and Pearson product-moment correlation. The post-lunch session resulted in greater driving fatigue and worse performance compared to pre-lunch as shown by higher KSS and PERCLOS level and longer reaction time. Significant changes of KSS were only observed in pre-lunch session whereas significant changes of reaction time were only observed in post-lunch indicating a different sensitivity of the two variables. PERCLOS, on the other hand, shows significant changes in both pre- and post-lunch. In correlation analysis, the number of data affects the correlation coefficient as insignificances were observed when the group of data was divided into pre- and post-lunch compared to the total data. As such, future study should involve more subjects using additional measurement systems to get reliable data are important for the development of a fatigue detection system.

articleTitle: Preface
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: On behalf of the Organizing Committee of the 6th International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA 2018), I would like to invite you all to attend this scientific conference. We hope this conference can provide an interesting program and serve as an excellent forum for innovative and technical discussion. In this year, the deputyship of engineering sciences of Indonesian Institute of Sciences (LIPI) accommodates eight international conferences under Indonesian Science Festival 2018. One of the conferences is ICSEEA 2018, which is held from 1st to 2nd November 2018 in ICE BSD City, Tangerang, Banten, Indonesia. The technical co-sponsor is IEEE Indonesian Section and this conference is organized by Research Center for Electrical Power and Mechatronics (RCEPM-LIPI). This conference is assigned for international scientists, technologists, researchers, academicians, government officials, practitioners and private sectors to interact and promote networking as well as expands their science and technology collaboration. Under the theme “Recent Research on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application” the conference performed new frontiers of sustainable energy engineering and application as a means for improving, developing and enriching human life. ICSEEA 2018 received 48 papers from 5 countries, out of which, 32 were accepted for oral presentation (only 31 of them will finally be submitted to IEEE for various reasons).
